links.targetTitle: Obex calculates its own rebate but Operational GovOps holds

title: Rebate eligibility is tied to custody: all other-Agent tokens must sit in Launch Agent 7's SubProxy account
content:
The first step of the Upkeep Rebate routine protocol is a custody rule, not a calculation: "Launch Agent 7 keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account" (A.6.1.1.8.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1).

The SubProxy address is published in the Artifact itself (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.3.1.1.2), so the rule makes the rebate base externally observable. Anyone — Operational GovOps, another Agent, a token holder — can read the balance at a known address and check it against the rebate the Agent claimed. The word "all" is what does the work: partial custody would let an Agent present a favourable subset of its holdings.

This is a general design move worth extracting: where a financial entitlement depends on a private fact, the Artifact converts the fact into a public one by constraining *where* the assets live rather than by demanding disclosure of them.

The cost is operational rigidity. An Agent that would otherwise deploy other Agents' tokens across strategies, custodians, or chains must keep them in one account to retain the rebate — the ecosystem is buying auditability with the Agent's balance-sheet flexibility.
description: Concentrating holdings in one publicly known address turns a claim about what the Agent holds into something an external reviewer can verify on-chain rather than take on trust.
